summary:
Most small farms in Africa depend on rain, and the rain is getting harder to predict. Each season, a farmer must decide what to plant with very little advice that fits their own land. SciFarm gives them a starting point.

You tap your farm on a map and answer two or three picture questions. SciFarm then offers three crop-rotation routes: one safe, one that rebuilds the soil, and one aimed at income. Each route shows why it was chosen and what happens in a dry, normal or wet year. The app works in English and French, reads answers aloud, and needs no login.

Everything is built on 45 years of NASA POWER climate data for 2,669 places across Africa, with open soil, crop and FAO data. A Data Passport shows the source of every number, and a Proof page tests our hazard index against five real events, including one we missed.

Scifarm helps a small rain-fed farmer in Africa decide what to plant.
